summary: Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1953–1962). He held multiple posts there, including professor (1964), dean (1991), and president (2009), and was also a professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Kouda served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Otani University, where he also held a post, and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 1976).
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University. He later served there as professor emeritus from around 1973 to 1992.

Ryoshun Okubo (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After studying at Waseda University (~1973–1982), he became a professor there around 1999 and holds posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and ICPBS (attested 2026).

Ryosuke Furui (born 1971) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and was appointed professor at the University of Tokyo in 2020 (attested there in 2011).
Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2015, he was a doctoral student and graduate student researcher at Toyo University and a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Shibuya was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.
Ryoun Yamada (born 1940) studied at Harvard Business School (~1969–1971) and worked in banking and corporate sectors. In Buddhist studies, he became the leader (Leiter) of Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii specializes in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii was a JSPS research fellow (attested 2003) and taught at Kokushikan University (attested 2010) and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).
Ryudo Suita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2010) and was affiliated with the university in 2020.

Ryugen Taga (born 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (graduating in 1955). He spent his academic career at Rissho University, serving as lecturer (attested 1961), professor (attested 1983), and president (attested 1993).

Ryugen Tanemura (born 1970) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held teaching posts at Taisho University (attested 2014–2026) and Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), and served as a researcher at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014).

Ryuichi Abe (born 1954) studied at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia under Yoshito S. Hakeda and Philip Boas Yampolsky. A scholar of Buddhism and Japanese religions, he taught at Columbia (1991–2004) before becoming a professor at Harvard University around 2006.

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1974) studied Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies under Sylvain Lévi. He was a regular contributor to Hōbōgirin, a professor at Tohoku University (attested 1953; professor emeritus attested 1972–1973), and head of Musashino University (attested 1963).

Ryuken Nawa is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who serves as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as professor emeritus at Taisho University and advisor at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (both attested 2014).
Ryuo (1856–1926) was a Buddhist studies scholar who taught at To-ji and Koyasan University.
Ryusei Keira specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, completing a thesis at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Tom Tillemans in 2003.
Ryushin Kitao (born 1941) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2014 and 2026).
